final_answer:
PRIVILEGED - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
MEMORANDUM: Issue Identification, Pinnacle's MSJ. Greenfield v. Pinnacle, No. 5:23-cv-00412-MTT (M.D. Ga.)
Reviewed: MSJ memo and SUMF (7/15/24), LSA, Okafor and Ellington declarations, Holt/Santos/Ellington deposition excerpts, Venkatesh report summary. Not in file (cites to them unverified): Hargrove, Yun, Okafor transcripts; Answer; Overstreet Exs. A-H.

BOTTOM LINE
The motion misquotes the LSA, relies on a record its own witness (Holt) contradicts, and uses an expert who conceded he is unqualified on salvageability. The cap and consequential-waiver arguments fail on the contract's actual text; force majeure fails on notice and causation; mitigation, comparative fault and damages are fact disputes. Lead theme: Pinnacle's gross negligence and concealment, which lifts the LSA limits and defeats SJ on credibility.

PRIORITY 1 - MISQUOTED CONTRACT (dispositive)

1. Cap (LSA 7.1). The memo quotes "in no event ... exceed the total fees paid ... twelve months preceding the date the claim first arose." Actual 7.1: liability "shall not exceed the greater of (a) the total fees paid ... during the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (b) $2,000,000. This limitation shall not apply to claims arising from Pinnacle's gross negligence or willful misconduct."
- Floor is $2,000,000, not $1,860,000. The carve-out is omitted from the memo and SUMF 11, 43.
- 7.2 also exempts Pinnacle's 9.1 indemnity (breach of 4.1-4.6; inventory contamination; attorneys' fees) and "claims for which Pinnacle is required to maintain insurance under Article 6." 6.1(b) requires all-risk property insurance on Greenfield Inventory at full replacement value. Memo ignores 7.2, 9.1, Art. 6. Demand the policies.
- Fee base is inconsistent: memo uses Feb 2022-Jan 2023; SUMF 14 uses July 2022-June 2023; Ellington Decl. 28 says "over the term"; SUMF 15 says Jan-Feb 2023 fees were withheld; 5.4 allows escalation.

2. Consequential waiver (7.3). Memo and SUMF 12 quote two different, non-LSA versions (including "regardless of foreseeability"). Actual: "Neither party shall be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages. This waiver shall not apply to claims arising from a party's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of Section 4.2." Every claim here is breach of 4.2 (60% RH, monitoring, monthly reports). Argument C ($2.04M) fails on the text. Also, replacement/expedite costs are arguably direct damages. Georgia's consequential-damages statute is O.C.G.A. 13-6-8; the memo cites it for mitigation (mitigation is 13-6-5).

3. Force majeure (11.7). The memo's block quote omits the conditions: notice "within 72 hours," written notice of the event, duration, obligations affected and steps taken, and ongoing updates. Holt: nobody notified Greenfield of the June, August or January failures; he "wasn't thinking about the force majeure clause" (Holt 29-30, 41, 85). SUMF 13 adds a "rendered impracticable" sentence not in 11.7.

PRIORITY 2 - FACT DISPUTES AND ADMISSIONS

4. Gross negligence/willful misconduct (lifts cap and 7.3 waiver). Holt:
- Aug. 9, 2022 email (Ex. 14): "We really need to replace the whole unit ... Greenfield's panels are in C and D and I'm worried about humidity." Okafor: "Get another patch. Replacement not in the budget until Q1 2023." Concerns raised 4-5 times; answer always "not in the budget" (Holt 38-45; logs Ex. 19).
- No dehumidifiers during the 14-day June outage, 13-day August outage, or the 2.5-3 week post-Jan. 18 outage (Holt 29-30, 83). Oct. 3 reading 78% RH; Nov.-Jan. readings upper 60s-70s.
- Okafor told Holt to withhold Nov.-Jan. reports because data showed non-compliance: "No point in raising alarms" (Holt 65-68, 99). SUMF 25 concedes no reports.
- Georgia defines gross negligence as lack of even slight diligence (O.C.G.A. 51-1-4); the LSA itself carves it out. Intent and diligence are jury questions.

5. Okafor declaration. Decl. 7 blames "calibration" for missing reports and says she does not recall instructing withholding; Holt says the opposite, so credibility defeats SJ (Anderson, 477 U.S. at 255). Decl. 5 cites lead times for not replacing; her email says "budget." Decl. 6 calls Oct. 3 "a single data point." The declaration has only 12 paragraphs; the memo cites Decl. 4 for regional facilities' climate problems (not there) and Decl. 8-9 for reports "fulfilled in the ordinary course" (not there). The "regional strain" fact has no record support. Decl. 11's denial of gross negligence is a legal conclusion.

6. Weather. SUMF 17: only 2-4F above the 30-year average; SUMF 22 and Holt 103: no power outage, so no "utility failure." "Record-breaking" has no record support. Georgia's act of God means irresistible physical cause excluding human agency (O.C.G.A. 1-3-3), and a bailee must show its own negligence did not contribute (44-12-45). Holt 101 and Venkatesh 5.3: refrigerant leaks, compressor failure, age, deferred maintenance. Failures after August fall outside the heat window. Pinnacle chose patches over replacement and dehumidifiers, so "commercially reasonable efforts" is itself disputed.

7. Mitigation. LSA 7.4 requires "commercially reasonable steps ... under the circumstances then known" and imposes no duty "to discover a breach that the other Party has concealed or failed to disclose in accordance with its reporting or notification obligations." 4.2 makes reports an "affirmative" obligation not conditioned on inspection; 4.5 inspection is "in addition to, and not in lieu of" reporting. That is exactly this case. Mitigation (13-6-5) is Pinnacle's burden.
- Santos: visits were logistics, not inspections (Santos 24-29); he asked Holt about missing reports in December and January and was told they were "coming" (33-38); no one disclosed HVAC problems before Feb. 6. Ellington Decl. 20 ("did not request the missing reports") is false.
- Santos page cites do not match the excerpts (memo 47:3-12, 48:15-22; SUMF 15:6-12, 28:4-10; excerpts show 24-29, 45-51). SUMF 30 (no 48-hour notice) is irrelevant. SUMF 23 ("access to data at all times") ignores the notice requirement and that data stopped. SUMF 27 admits Greenfield relied on the reports. Venkatesh 5.8: timely reports would have allowed relocation to Zones A/B (48-55% RH).

8. Comparative fault (O.C.G.A. 51-12-33). A tort apportionment statute; the memo cites no contract authority against Count I. S. Gen. Ins. Co. v. Holt, 262 Ga. 267 (1992) is an insurer bad-faith failure-to-settle case, not apportionment (verified). Denton v. Eaton unverified. No evidence Greenfield owed or breached a duty to inspect, and no basis for 50%+ fault; allocation is for the jury. Confirm Pinnacle pleaded mitigation, comparative fault and force majeure (Rule 8(c)); Answer not in file.

9. Counts II and III. The memo makes no count-specific argument, so Pinnacle has not carried its Celotex burden. Our risk: a reply raising the economic-loss rule or that the implied covenant is not freestanding; prepare independent-duty and good-faith facts.

PRIORITY 3 - EXPERT AND DAMAGES

10. Ellington (Fed. R. Evid. 702, as amended Dec. 1, 2023; Daubert motion and motion to strike).
- Admissions (Dep. 14, 78-85): no science, mold, IICRC credentials; never remediated wood panels; did not review S520 or any peer-reviewed study; on salvageability "I would defer" to Venkatesh, who found the panels non-salvageable. Pinnacle has no competing industrial hygienist.
- Shifting numbers: incremental cost per panel $1,750 (MSJ), $1,680 (Decl. 13), about $1,780 (Dep. 42); salvageable share 35-45% (MSJ), 30-40% (Decl. 14), 25-30% (Dep. 43). MSJ's salvage figure ($1.645-2.115M) uses full cost; the declaration uses $1,680; salvage and overhead reductions double count.
- Credentials differ: Halford MBA 2001, Georgia Tech BSIE, 22 years, 15 cases (Decl.) versus Emory MBA, UVA economics, 18 years, 12 cases (Dep.). The deposition describes "Warehouse 7 in Perry" and "Robert Santos." A declaration dated after the deposition cannot contradict it (Van T. Junkins & Assocs. v. U.S. Indus., 736 F.2d 656 (11th Cir. 1984), from general knowledge).
- Mitigation opinion assumes degradation began mid-September 2022 (Decl. 22), contradicting the June/August failures; he did not address the missing reports (Dep. 93-95). "Consequential" labels are legal conclusions (Dep. 46).
- His own adjusted range ($1.728-2.254M, Decl. 27) concedes substantial damages. Overhead exclusion is a measure-of-damages dispute for trial.
- The memo attributes to him a "shelf-life" opinion; Decl. 25 says overtime was routine and $180,000 of shipping was unrelated.

11. Venkatesh is unrebutted: hyphae in 34/36 tape lifts and 18/18 swabs; moisture 22-35%; warping about 60%, delamination about 40%; Stachybotrys; S520/EPA; Zones A/B clean. Use the full report.

12. Fees and lost profits. The memo cites 13-6-5 for litigation expenses; correct is 13-6-11. The $175,000 Linden fees may be indemnified "Losses" (LSA 1.7, 9.1, including attorneys' fees); concealment supports 13-6-11. Our risk: Venkatesh disclaims lost-profit opinions (6.4); confirm a damages witness and documents for Tri-County, Peach State, Heritage.

PRIORITY 4 - RECORD AND CITATION DEFECTS

13. The memo's SUMF cites do not match: weather is SUMF 17 (memo 13-14); HVAC 18-21 (memo 15-19); damages 40-42 (memo 36-40); experts 38-39 (memo 41-43); SUMF 14 is fees, cited for Georgia Power "strain." Aug. 8 vs 9; third "repair" in late Sept vs Oct. 3/11; Jan. 18, 2023 failure omitted. Non-renewal notice stated as 90 days (LSA 2.1: 180). LSA section cites in SUMF 5-7, 11-14 are wrong. SUMF 32 says Yun was notified; memo says CEO. "Brian Holt" (SUMF 16) is Derek Holt. Venkatesh appears as "Anisha" and elsewhere "Subramanian"; the "Ellington Report (Jan. 15, 2024)" carries Venkatesh's date. Counsel bar numbers differ across filings. Respond under Fed. R. Civ. P. 56(c) and M.D. Ga. L.R. 56 paragraph by paragraph (deny SUMF 11-14, 23, 31, 43, 45 as misquoted or unsupported), object under 56(c)(2), and file our own fact statement.

14. Authority. Barton Protective v. Faber, 274 Ga. App. 737: only a Florida 1999 case located. Royal Ins. v. Crowne, 903 F.2d 806 (11th Cir.): only an Alabama 2004 case located (903 So. 2d 802); the cite appears fabricated or garbled. Ga. Power v. Roper, 201 Ga. App. 283: only a 1947 case (74 Ga. App. 750) located. Hardin, Toncee, Denton not verified. O.C.G.A. 11-2-715 is UCC sales, not a services/bailment contract. Celotex, Anderson, Matsushita are real.

OPPOSITION STRUCTURE
(1) LSA's actual text (7.1 floor and carve-outs, 7.2, 7.3 carve-out, 7.4, 11.7). (2) Holt/Okafor concealment as gross negligence and credibility. (3) Mitigation and comparative fault. (4) Rule 702 challenge; Venkatesh unrebutted. (5) Counter-statement of facts. Gather: Exs. 14, 19, other Holt-Okafor emails, Blackthorn quotes, Pinnacle insurance policies, damages back-up, missing transcripts.

Caveat: gross-negligence cap exception, sham-affidavit rule and the Rule 702 amendment are stated from general knowledge; cite-check before filing.
